description: Compilers, test runners, and linters. Safe to allow broadly even though e.g. `node -e "..."` / `python -c "..."` can run arbitrary interpreted code we can't statically inspect: these run as ONE self-contained Bash call, so the kernel sandbox (bubblewrap) normally stays ON and enforces filesystem/network containment on whatever the interpreter actually does, regardless of what this argv-level rule can see. `sandboxOverride` is inert unless the project sets `allowUnsandboxedCommands` (see the 006 migration) — the escape hatch for a project whose tests must reach host-local services over raw TCP, which no amount of proxy routing can deliver. Turning it on for a project makes this category filter-only, which is exactly as wide as it sounds. See docs/SANDBOX-FINDINGS.md.
